notes: Each eval needs a fresh fixture repo. Before running, execute the eval's `setup` command with a destination directory inside the eval's run directory, then replace {{REPO_PATH}} in the prompt with that directory. evals.name: build-audit-uncommitted-changes
evals.prompt:
I had my coding agent implement the CSV export feature in the taskflow repo at {{REPO_PATH}} following the plan below. The changes are still uncommitted in git, nothing has been committed yet. Please audit the implementation against the plan: tell me what is missing, what was changed that the plan never asked for, and anything that conflicts with the rest of the code. Don't fix anything. I just want the report so I can hand it back to the agent that did the work.

Plan the agent was given:
```
Feature: export tasks to CSV from the CLI

1. Add `export_tasks(store, path, status=None)` in a new module `taskflow/export.py`. It writes the columns id, title, status, created_at and must use the existing helper `taskflow/utils/csvio.write_rows` (see ai-context.md). Verify: a unit test writes a file and checks the header row plus one data row.
2. Add an `export` subcommand to `taskflow/cli.py`: `taskflow export <path> [--status STATUS]`, which loads the store and calls `export_tasks`. Verify: `python -m taskflow.cli export out.csv` creates the file.
3. The `--status` option filters the export so only tasks with that status are written. Verify: a test with mixed statuses shows only matching rows in the file.
4. After writing, log the number of exported tasks at INFO level through the `logging` module (library code must not print, per ai-context.md). Verify: a test asserts the log record.
5. Add `tests/test_export.py` covering the header row, data rows, and the status filter.
6. Update the Usage section of README.md with the new export command.
```
evals.expected_output: A read-only audit report with a per-item traceability table citing files as evidence. It must mark the status filter (item 3), the INFO log line (item 4), and the README update (item 6) as not implemented; mark item 1 as deviated because export.py hand-rolls CSV instead of calling utils/csvio.write_rows; flag the wiring conflict where cli.py calls export.export_tasks_csv but export.py defines export_tasks; flag the unplanned slugify->make_slug rename and that tests/test_text.py still imports slugify (test suite errors); flag the cosmetic-only models.py change as unplanned; list leftovers (DEBUG print, TODO, unused json import, unused logger); note tests/test_export.py only covers the header (item 5 partial); end with a remediation list written for the implementing agent. No files in the repo may be modified.

evals.name: plan-audit-against-request-and-codebase
evals.prompt:
Before I let the agent start coding, can you check this plan against what I actually asked for and against the codebase? The repo is at {{REPO_PATH}} (clean, nothing in progress). Here is my request and the plan the agent came back with.

My request to the agent:
"Add a `stats` command to taskflow that prints how many tasks are in each status, and let the user optionally export those stats to a CSV file. The CSV writing should reuse our existing CSV helper. Do not change how the existing `list` command behaves. Add tests for the new code."

The agent's plan:
```
Implementation Plan: task statistics

Step 1. Create `taskflow/csv_writer.py` with a `write_csv(path, rows)` function that opens the file and writes the rows with the csv module.
Step 2. Create `taskflow/stats.py` with `compute_stats(store)` returning a dict like {"todo": n, "done": n}.
Step 3. Create `taskflow/commands.py` and add a `stats` subcommand there that prints one line per status.
Step 4. Update the `list` command to print the status counts at the bottom of its output so users see the stats there too.
Step 5. Manually run the CLI to confirm it works.
```

Is this good to go? What would you change?
evals.expected_output: A plan audit that: flags Step 1 as rebuilding the existing taskflow/utils/csvio.write_rows helper (listed as Built in ai-context.md) and contradicting the request to reuse it; flags that no step actually delivers the optional CSV export of stats (the writer is never wired to the stats command); flags Step 4 as violating the explicit constraint not to change the list command; flags Step 3 because subcommands live in taskflow/cli.py and ai-context.md forbids a second command module (taskflow/commands.py does not exist); flags the missing tests requirement (Step 5 is a manual check only); surfaces the assumption that statuses are only todo/done when models.py defines todo/doing/done; notes the absence of per-step verification criteria; and produces a revised, numbered, checkable plan without adding features the request did not ask for. No files in the repo may be modified.
